From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Hosted vs Dedicated  latency/throughput recommendation and benchmarks

Hi Alex / Marissa  thanks for the packet and context. Quick technical readout after reviewing the payload sizes and burst profile you shared: 

Short answer: Hosted API can meet the 60ms p99 for typical auth requests under moderate load with our optimizations (prefix caching + continuous batching + dynamic kernel selection). However, for sustained 100 rps with repeated 500 rps bursts and a hard p99 SLA, Dedicated capacity is recommended to guarantee predictable tail latency and to provide isolation during noisy-neighbor events.

Key notes:
- Latency assumptions: our internal benchmark for similar payloads (350 tokens in / 30 tokens out) shows p50 ~2030ms, p95 ~4055ms, p99 ~6590ms on Hosted under mixed traffic. Adding KV prefix caching for common auth prompts reduces p99 by ~1020ms in many cases.
- Throughput: Hosted autoscaling is fast, but there is variability during multi-minute bursts; Dedicated with reserved GPU pools provides headroom and consistent p99 under burst.
- Cost tradeoff: Dedicated lowers per-token unit cost at scale but requires a monthly commitment; Hosted is pay-as-you-go and faster to start. We'll include a 30/60/90-day pilot pricing comparison in the SOW.
- Compliance: For US-only data residency + audit log exports, Dedicated with our VPC peering option or Private deployment is simplest to document for procurement. Hosted can be configured with region restrictions but may need additional contract terms.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_summary.xlsx (includes benchmark runs that match your payload; see tabs: hosted_baseline, dedicated_baseline, caching_effects).

Requested from FinPay to finalize recommendation:
1) Sample request/response JSON (anonymized) for 50100 requests so we can run a quick internal pilot.
2) Confirmation of burst windows and whether bursts are predictable/scheduled.
3) Any contract constraints (e.g., preferred billing cadence or required SLAs).

If it helps, we can spin up a small dedicated pilot (2 GPUs reserved) and run a controlled burst test within 10 business days. Happy to walk through the attached benchmark in the call  I can do Fri 2/13 09:00 PST.

Best,
